# MM-P2-L2-IH01-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01

Scope
- This maintenance manual section defines lubrication and permitted fluids for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01). It covers background, rationale for lubrication and fluid checks, coil inspection cadence, permissible lubricant part number, procedure for lubricant application and fluid handling, records to retain, and acceptance criteria for service completion.
- This document is to be used in conjunction with referenced procedures and safety bulletins: MM-P2-L2-IH01, SB-1024, SOP-P2-L2-01.

Background and rationale
- The induction billet heater coil and ancillary moving or sealing elements require controlled lubrication to maintain electrical and mechanical performance and to prevent premature wear, arcing, or contamination of the heated billet path.
- Lubrication choice is based on compatibility with electrical components and high-resistance prevention. The authorized lubricant for this unit is listed to ensure traceability and consistency across maintenance actions.
- Regular coil inspection reduces the risk of unexpected downtime by identifying insulation degradation, loose terminations, or conductive deposits that can lead to failure. The coil inspection interval for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 365 hours. This interval must be tracked in maintenance logs and aligned with production schedules using SOP-P2-L2-01.

Tools
- Personal protective equipment as required by SB-1024 and site PPE policy; consult SOP-P2-L2-01 for lockout/tagout and hot work controls.
- Insulation resistance meter suitable for induction equipment (consult MM-P2-L2-IH01 for model selection guidance).
- Non-conductive cleaning brushes and lint-free wipes.
- Approved solvent or cleaner consistent with electrical equipment cleaning; reference MM-P2-L2-IH01 for approved chemistries.
- Applicator suitable for controlled dispensing of lubricant to avoid over-application.
- Waste collection containers and absorbents in compliance with site environmental procedures.
- Maintenance log or electronic maintenance system entry form.

Approved fluids and parts
- Lubricant: CFW-LUB-938. Use only CFW-LUB-938 for the components specified in this document. The lubricant provides the required film properties while being compatible with adjacent insulation and sealing materials.
- For any fluid not explicitly listed in this document, obtain approval per MM-P2-L2-IH01 before use.

Procedure
- Prepare: Coordinate with operations per SOP-P2-L2-01 to schedule a maintenance window. Follow SB-1024 for all safety precautions, isolation, and energization controls. Verify lockout/tagout is in place and voltage is verified absent before accessing coil or electrical terminations.
- Inspect visual condition of coil assembly, support insulators, and termination points. Look for discoloration, cracking of insulation, loose connections, or conductive residues. If contaminants are present, clean using non-conductive cleaner per MM-P2-L2-IH01 and allow components to dry fully before further inspection.
- Test insulation resistance across the coil and to ground with the insulation resistance meter. Compare readings to acceptance criteria referenced in MM-P2-L2-IH01. If values are outside accepted ranges, escalate per MM-P2-L2-IH01.
- Lubricate mechanical sliding interfaces, bearings, and seals identified in the equipment maintenance diagram using CFW-LUB-938. Apply minimal quantity necessary to achieve a continuous film without excess drip or transfer to the heated billet path. Use an applicator to control deposit location. Avoid application on electrical terminations or on surfaces that contact the billet.
- After lubrication, rotate or actuate the component through its normal range to distribute the lubricant evenly. Observe for any leakage, unusual resistance to movement, or transfer of lubricant into areas where it may contact hot metal.
- Re-inspect coil area for any lubricant overspray or residues. If lubricant is found on electrical surfaces or within the coil window, clean immediately with approved non-conductive cleaner and re-verify insulation resistance.
- Restore equipment to service following SOP-P2-L2-01 energization and warm-up procedures. Monitor first production pieces for signs of oil transfer, smoke, or abnormal readings; if detected, de-energize and correct.
- Frequency and scheduling: Record the date and meter hours at completion. The coil inspection interval for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 365 hours; schedule the next inspection in the maintenance system accordingly.

Examples and step rationale
- Example scenario: If a technician finds light discoloration at a coil termination but insulation resistance remains within acceptable range per MM-P2-L2-IH01, the technician should perform a targeted cleaning and apply lubrication to nearby mechanical supports only, then re-check resistance before return to service. This approach avoids unnecessary part replacement while preserving electrical integrity.
- Rationale: Limiting lubricant type to CFW-LUB-938 prevents chemical incompatibilities that can degrade insulation varnish or create conductive films when exposed to high temperatures. Minimal application prevents migration into the heated billet path.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry including date, technician name, description of actions taken, readings from insulation resistance meter, part number of lubricant used (CFW-LUB-938), and meter hours at service completion.
- Attach or reference any photos taken during inspection and cleaning in the maintenance record.
- Record any deviations from this procedure and justification, with reference to MM-P2-L2-IH01 for approval steps.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil visual inspection reveals no open or cracked insulation that would expose conductive surfaces; any marginal conditions documented and approved per MM-P2-L2-IH01.
- Post-service insulation resistance readings meet the acceptance bands defined in MM-P2-L2-IH01. If not, remedial action is required before return to service.
- Lubricant used is documented as CFW-LUB-938 and applied such that no lubricant is present on electrical terminations or inside the coil window.
- No oil transfer or smoking observed during initial production after service. If any of these are observed, stop production and perform corrective action per MM-P2-L2-IH01 and SOP-P2-L2-01.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L2-IH01
- SB-1024
- SOP-P2-L2-01
